title: Service Advisor - Volkswagen Shrewsbury
description:
Service Advisor - Volkswagen Shrewsbury

Good, honest, rewarding work. It's how we're built.

In the heart of our aftersales department our Service Advisors are committed to delivering outstanding and trusted experiences for our customers. As a Service Advisor you are the main point of contact for all customer communication while the vehicle is undergoing maintenance and repair in our Retail Centre.

As part of a successful, global automotive group, you'll broaden your experience across both sites and brands. And with the right support from us, you'll be able to progress as high as you can aim.

What we can offer you
- Enjoy 33 days of annual leave (including bank holidays) to rest and recharge
- Save money every day with our exclusive retail discounts
- Drive a great deal with discounts on new and used cars, plus servicing offers
- Plan for the years ahead with our company pension scheme
- Balance home and work with our industry-leading family-friendly policies designed to help you spend more time with the people that matter
- Commute for less with our cycle-to-work scheme
- Prioritise your wellbeing with dedicated support for you and your family
- 24/7 access to healthcare professionals, ensuring you get the expert advice you need quickly and easily
- Make a difference with a paid day to volunteer in your community
- Invest in your future with our company share purchase plan
- Earn financial rewards when you refer a friend to join the team
- Keep learning and growing with our training and development opportunities for everyone.
- Life assurance with the option to increase cover
- We're open to flexible working options - just ask

What you'll do day to day
- Warmly welcome and engage customers in a friendly and professional manner throughout the day
- Keep customers informed and updated on the progress of their vehicle repairs, ensuring transparency and trust
- Develop and maintain comprehensive product knowledge, enhancing expertise through manufacturer-led training
- Actively promote additional services and repairs based on Technician recommendations, helping customers maintain vehicle health and increasing service revenue
- Schedule vehicles for appointments in the workshop efficiently and accurately
- Conduct pre-appointment customer calls to confirm bookings, ensure readiness, and address any preliminary questions
- Maintain precise and up-to-date customer records within our systems for effective service management

Helpful skills and qualifications

Don't worry about ticking off every single skill here if you care about delivering great experiences as much as we do, we want to hear from you.
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with customers and colleagues
- Demonstrated experience in delivering exceptional customer service
- Skilled at identifying customer needs and opportunities for upselling
- Excellent time management skills and the ability to work under pressure
- Previous experience in a target driven role, demonstrating the ability to meet goals
- Must hold a valid UK driving licence

We value diversity and believe it strengthens our team. If you don't meet every requirement listed but are enthusiastic about this role and eager to learn, we encourage you to apply.

Be part of something big

Group 1 Automotive is on an exciting growth journey. We are home to over 7000 colleagues dedicated to providing exceptional customer service, with 114 dealerships in the UK, representing 21 brands at the forefront of automotive retail.

But you don't need to love cars to work with us - just need to share our mission to create outstanding and trusted experiences for our customers, our partners, and our people.

Our Values

At Group 1 Automotive we pride ourselves on our five core values that are incorporated in all we that do.

Respect - Integrity - Transparency - Teamwork - Professionalism

These are the principles that every member of our team lives by, whether that be business functions, customer interactions, how we interact with the local community and even how we view each other in the team.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Cosgrove & Cosgrove Ltd Telford, Shropshire

£28,000-£30,000 per annum depending on experience Full-time Permanent Office-based

Cosgrove & Cosgrove is looking for an experienced Accounts Assistant to join our small finance team in Telford, supporting the day-to-day accounts across multiple businesses.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys keeping accurate records, resolving queries and taking ownership of their work. You should be confident completing bank reconciliations independently and managing a varied workload without constant supervision.

What you'll be doing
- Completing bank reconciliations independently across multiple accounts and investigating discrepancies.
- Maintaining purchase and sales ledgers, processing supplier invoices, and raising and processing sales invoices.
- Processing expenses and credit card transactions, matching receipts and following up missing information.
- Using Dext to support invoice and receipt processing.
- Carrying out bookkeeping and data entry, keeping QuickBooks Online records accurate and up to date.
- Preparing and posting journals, including payroll journals, and collating payroll information.
- Liaising with colleagues and suppliers to resolve queries.
- Supporting month-end tasks and the wider finance team.

What we're looking for
- At least two years' practical UK accounts or bookkeeping experience.
- The ability to complete bank reconciliations independently.
- Practical experience of purchase and sales ledgers, supplier invoices and expenses.
- Good Excel skills and practical experience using QuickBooks Online. Both are essential.
- Strong attention to detail, good organisation and the ability to prioritise your workload.
- A reliable commute to our Telford office for this fully office-based role.

Experience using Dext would be an advantage. An AAT qualification or progress towards one would be useful, but is not essential; practical experience and the ability to do the work are what matter.

How to apply

Please submit your CV and include a short covering note answering the following:
- How many years of practical UK accounts or bookkeeping experience do you have?
- How many years have you used QuickBooks Online, and have you used Dext?
- What experience do you have of preparing payroll information and posting payroll journals?
- How would you describe your Excel level? Please give examples of the functions or tasks you use regularly.
- What are you looking for in your next role and why are you leaving your current position? If you are not currently employed, please tell us what you are looking for next.
- What is your notice period or earliest available start date?

title: Customer Service Administrator
description:
Role Details

Role: Property Manager

Location: Shrewsbury

Salary: £28,000-£31,000

Role Overview

Durrant Talent Solutions is proud to be partnering with a leading national residential managing agent in the search for a Property Manager to join their Shrewsbury team.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Property Manager to take ownership of a residential portfolio, delivering exceptional property management services while building strong relationships with leaseholders, residents, clients and contractors.

The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring developments are managed to the highest professional standards, maintaining compliance, overseeing maintenance and service delivery, and providing an outstanding customer experience across their portfolio.

Role Responsibilities
- Manage a portfolio of residential leasehold developments.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with leaseholders, Resident Management Companies (RMCs), Right to Manage Companies (RTMs) and freeholder clients.
- Prepare and manage annual service charge budgets in conjunction with internal teams.
- Monitor expenditure and ensure developments are managed within approved budgets.
- Arrange, attend and chair site inspections and client meetings as required.
- Instruct, monitor and review contractors to ensure works are completed to the required standard.
- Oversee planned and reactive maintenance across the portfolio.
- Ensure compliance with all relevant health and safety legislation, including fire, asbestos, water hygiene and lift regulations.
- Work closely with internal departments including finance, compliance and customer services.
- Respond promptly and professionally to customer enquiries and resolve issues effectively.
- Ensure accurate property records are maintained and all administration is completed within agreed timescales.

Essential Experience

The successful candidate will have:
- Previous experience managing a residential block management portfolio.
- A good understanding of residential leasehold legislation and property management best practice.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage a varied workload.
- A proactive and customer-focused approach.
- The ability to prioritise tasks and work independently.
- Competent IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- A full UK driving licence (where required).

Desirable Experience
- TPI qualified or working towards level 3
- Experience using property management software such as Qube, TRAMPS, Propman or similar.

Equal Opportunities Statement

Durrant Talent Solutions is committed to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion throughout the recruitment process. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified individuals regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under the Equality Act 2010. Selection decisions are based solely on skills, experience, qualifications and suitability for the role.

Due to the high volume of applications received, we may only be able to contact candidates who are shortlisted. If you do not hear from us within 7 days of submitting your application, please assume your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.

title: Accounts & Finance Coordinator
description:
Accounts & Finance Coordinator (Part-Time)

Location - Shropshire (Rural Location) Fully office-based.
Hours- 16 hours per week initially. Flexible working pattern available:
- 2 full days per week, or
- 4 half days per week

Salary £15 per hour Freelance arrangements may be considered for the right candidate.
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced, organised and proactive Accounts & Finance Coordinator to join our growing client based in the beautiful rural location of South Shropshire.

This is a key position within the organisation, responsible for the day-to-day management and coordination of financial activities while supporting the leadership team with accurate financial information, planning and forecasting.

The successful candidate will play an important role in helping the business maintain strong financial controls and gain clear visibility of its financial position, both now and in the future.

Due to their rural location, applicants must be able to reliably travel to and work from our office. This is not a remote or hybrid position.
Key Responsibilities Bookkeeping & Financial Administration
- Maintain accurate financial records using Xero.
- Process sales and purchase invoices.
- Manage bank reconciliations and financial transactions.
- Maintain organised financial records and documentation.

Payroll & Compliance
- Process payroll accurately and in a timely manner.
- Prepare information for VAT returns.
- Ensure financial records remain compliant and audit-ready.
- Liaise with external accountants regarding financial reporting and compliance requirements.

Credit Control & Payments
- Manage customer accounts and credit control processes.
- Monitor outstanding balances and follow up on overdue payments.
- Process supplier payments and oversee payment schedules.
- Coordinate factory and stock-related payments.

Cash Flow & Financial Planning
- Monitor and forecast cash flow requirements.
- Assist with budgeting and financial planning.
- Track future financial commitments and upcoming expenditure.
- Provide management with regular financial updates and reports.

Stock & Business Planning As a stock-based business, financial planning around inventory and purchasing is particularly important. The successful candidate will:
- Monitor stock-related financial commitments.
- Support planning for stock purchases and replenishment.
- Assist with forecasting future expenditure.
- Help ensure sufficient cash availability for key business commitments.

Person Specification Essential Experience & Skills
- Proven experience in bookkeeping, finance administration or accounts management.
- Strong practical knowledge of Xero.
- Experience managing payroll, invoicing, reconciliations and financial reporting.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Strong numerical and analytical abilities.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- Confident communicating with suppliers, customers, accountants and management.
- Ability to work independently and take ownership of responsibilities.

Personal Attributes We are looking for someone who:
- Is highly organised and proactive.
- Takes pride in accuracy and attention to detail.
- Enjoys working as part of a small, collaborative team.
- Can build positive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
- Is comfortable working independently and making informed decisions within their area of responsibility.

Additional Information
- This role is fully office-based in Shropshire, a rural location requiring reliable transportation.
- Flexible working arrangements are available regarding how the 16 hours are worked each week.
- The role would suit an experienced finance professional seeking a part-time position that can fit around family or other commitments.
- There is genuine opportunity for the role, responsibilities and hours to develop as the business continues to grow.

title: Project Coordinator
description:
We are recruiting on behalf of a dynamic and growing organisation based in Shropshire that is looking for an experienced and highly organised Project Coordinator to join their team. This is a fantastic opportunity to step into a pivotal role within a business that is genuinely ambitious, fast-moving, and invested in the people who help drive it forward.

Working in a hybrid capacity, you will have the flexibility to split your time between the London office and home, while playing a central role in the coordination and delivery of key projects across the business. If you are someone who thrives on keeping multiple workstreams on track, communicating clearly with stakeholders, and making sure things get done to the highest standard, this role is for you.

What You Will Be Doing
- Leading the day-to-day coordination of projects from initiation through to successful delivery
- Managing project timelines, milestones, and deliverables, ensuring deadlines are consistently met
- Facilitating project meetings, capturing actions, and holding teams accountable for progress
- Maintaining comprehensive project documentation, risk registers, and status reports
- Acting as a central point of contact between internal teams, senior stakeholders, and external partners
- Proactively identifying risks, dependencies, and blockers - and escalating or resolving them swiftly
- Supporting resource planning, budget tracking, and reporting as required
- Contributing to the continuous improvement of project management processes and ways of working

What We Are Looking For
- Proven experience in a Project Coordinator, Project Manager, or similar delivery-focused role
- Strong understanding of project management methodologies (e.g. Agile, PRINCE2, or similar)
- Exceptional organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects
- Confident communicator - able to engage effectively with stakeholders at all levels, including senior leadership
- Proficient in project management tools such as Jira, Asana, MS Project, or equivalent
- A proactive, solutions-focused mindset with excellent attention to detail
- Comfortable working independently in a hybrid environment
- A relevant project management qualification (e.g. PRINCE2, APM, PMP) is desirable but not essential

What Is On Offer
- Hybrid working - a flexible split between the London office and home
- 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- A high-profile role with genuine influence over project outcomes and business direction
- Fantastic opportunities to grow within the organisation, with clear pathways for career progression
- Funded training and support for professional development and project management qualifications
- A collaborative, ambitious team culture where your contribution is recognised and rewarded

This organisation is recruiting directly through Consula, their recruitment partner.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: We are looking for an enthusiastic, reliable and patient-focused Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly GP practice team. The successful candidate will work as part of our reception team, supporting the safe and efficient preparation and supply of medicines to our patients. You will play an important role in ensuring that prescriptions are processed accurately, medicines are appropriately stored and stock levels are maintained. This is a busy and varied role, requiring excellent attention to detail, good organisational skills and a professional approach to patient care. Previous experience in a reception, office administration or GP practice environment would be advantageous. However, we are also interested in candidates with relevant transferable experience and a willingness to undertake appropriate training. The successful candidate will: Provide a friendly, professional and welcoming reception service to patients and visitors. Answer telephone calls and deal with patient enquiries promptly and courteously, ensuring queries are directed to the appropriate member of the practice team. Book, amend and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Support patients with general administrative and non-clinical queries.. Register new patients and maintain accurate patient records. Undertake general administrative duties, including scanning, filing, processing correspondence and updating records. Support clinicians and the wider practice team with day-to-day administrative tasks. Liaise with hospitals, pharmacies, community services and other healthcare organisations where appropriate. Maintain confidentiality and ensure patient information is handled securely and in accordance with practice policies and information governance requirements. Follow practice procedures relating to safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and confidentiality. Work effectively as part of a busy multidisciplinary team and contribute to the smooth running of the practice. Deal with patients in a respectful, sensitive and professional manner, including those who may be distressed or have additional needs. Undertake other reasonable administrative duties appropriate to the role. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients and visitors, supporting the smooth day-to-day operation of the practice. The post holder will work as part of the wider practice team, providing front-line support to patients, managing appointments and enquiries, maintaining accurate patient information and undertaking a range of administrative duties in accordance with practice policies, procedures and information governance requirements. The post holder will work within the limits of their training and competence and will refer clinical, complex or sensitive matters to the appropriate member of the practice team.

title: Admin Assistant/Receptionist
description: This role isnoteligible for visa sponsorship. We are looking for an Administrative Assistant to join our Adult Mental Health Services based in Severn Fields Health Village, Shrewsbury. The Service offers mental health care and treatment across a variety of different age ranges and presentation. The role is fixed term for 10 months and would require you to work 37.5 hours per week (Monday to Friday 9.00am to 5.00pm). You would predominantly be based in Severn Fields, although you may be required to travel to work in other Trust locations to meet service need. In the role you will be working as part of a team along with Administrative Assistants and Medical and Clinical Administrators. You will be expected to be able to use your own initiative and judgement, although you will be well supported by other Mental Health Admin staff and through the clinical and professional networks accessible through the community teams. The administration offices are busy, and the role is challenging but it is alsorewarding. To accurately maintain and keep secure patient health and staff records/systems in line with policy and standard operating procedure, to ensure data quality, confidentiality and compliance with the current Data Protection Law. Maintain strict confidentiality regarding information concerning patients, staff and sensitive Trust Business at all times. To carry out reception duties including meeting and greeting service users, carers, relatives and visitors, as requested by the Admin Support Supervisor and/or the Admin Team Leader. Handle incoming and outgoing telephone calls in a polite and efficient manner. Receive and deal with telephone enquiries referring telephone queries to a more senior colleague where appropriate. Taking accurate messages and passing them to the appropriate person in a timely manner. Type a range of documents including emailed requests, copy typing and audio transcription (via T-Pro digital dictation system) generated by the mental health pathway teams. Prioritise own workload and meet deadlines in order to meet the requirements of the post. Regular data entry and booking of appointments for service users on the clinical patient administration system, RiO. Take / transcribe minutes as required and at the request of the Admin Support Supervisor and/or Admin Team Leader. To work predominantly from a base, although travel to work in other Trust locations within the locality will be required to meet service need. For further information relating to this position please refer to the attached job description and specification. If you would like to chat in more detail about the position, please contact Sian Wallis: Sian.Wallis@mpft.nhs.uk
